# TCEC NNUE compliance

**Rule**: all training data must be generated by the engine's own search
and/or evaluation code. No external source (Stockfish, other engines,
human game databases) may contribute a label or a position to the
training data of a presented network.

## How it's upheld, phase by phase

**Openings (self-play)**: generated by Luna itself (random moves filtered
for "undecided" positions according to the evaluation — **Stockfish for
gen1**, gen1 network for gen2, gen2 network for gen3 — see note below).
For the endgame pool: real positions from `lichess_db_puzzle.csv`,
filtered only by piece count and material imbalance — no engine
evaluation involved in the selection, so no external label source there
either.

**Correction (2026-09-15)**: the **gen1** normal-opening
filter uses Stockfish (`pipeline/generate/gen_random_openings.py`, invoked
by `generate_shards_gen1.sh`), not the classical evaluation as this
document previously stated. This is a **selection** contamination of
starting positions, not a **label** one: no gen1 position or value
produced by self-play/annotation comes from Stockfish. From gen2 onward
the filter uses the previous generation's network (Luna itself) — correct
there. The residual external influence propagates only indirectly through
the gen1 network used as master for later generations: it attenuates with
each round, it does not compound. Full detail in `LINEAGE.md`, generation
1 section. Not fixed by regenerating (disproportionate cost: redoing gen1
would mean redoing gen2 and gen3 too) — declared, not hidden.

**Self-play**: Luna-against-Luna games, evaluated by its own network (or
classical PST for gen1), never Stockfish, never akimbo as a player.

**Labels**: the evaluation (`eval_cp`) and best move (`bestmove`) of every
position come from Luna's own SEARCH (`go nodes N`) with the current
generation's master network — never from Stockfish, never from a
third-party engine.

**WDL resolution for truncated games**: uses the `eval_cp` already written
by Luna in the same annotation pass — calls no external engine.

## The grep trap, defused

Searching the repository for "stockfish" **will** find it, in several
places. This is the complete list of every file where it appears (not
just the convenient ones), with each one's real category — **a table that
lists the uncomfortable occurrences too is more credible than one that
only lists the innocuous ones**.

| Category | Files | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Calls Stockfish as a label source** (non-compliant) | `non_conforme/annotate_positions.py`, `non_conforme/annotate_incremental_gen0.py`, `non_conforme/_annotate_chunk_worker_gen0.py` | These are gen0 — isolated in `non_conforme/` by construction, never part of the gen1+ pipeline. See `non_conforme/README.md`. |
| **Calls Stockfish to filter openings** (selection, not a label — gen1 only) | `pipeline/generate/gen_random_openings.py`, `pipeline/generate/generate_shards_gen1.sh` | Contamination declared in `LINEAGE.md` (generation 1) and above in this document. Not removed: declared. |
| **Comments only, no call** (explicitly say "not Stockfish") | `pipeline/annotate/annotate_incremental_gen1.py`, `pipeline/annotate/_annotate_chunk_worker_gen1.py`, `pipeline/train/train.py`, `pipeline/train/dataset.py` | Compliant code that says so in its own comment — not a suspicious occurrence. |
| **Metric / provenance values** (historical numbers written as data, not calls) | `pipeline/generate/write_manifest_gen2.py`, `pipeline/generate/write_manifest_gen3.py`, all 99 files under `manifests/gen1/` and `manifests/gen2/` | Fields like `gen1_spearman_vs_stockfish: 0.5874` — a measurement number recorded in the manifest, not an engine invocation. |
| **Offline measurement tool** (reads or produces a reference value, never writes to training data) | `results/scripts/measure_static_vs_stockfish.py`, `results/scripts/measure_search_vs_stockfish.py`, `pipeline/measure/measure_master_spearman.py`, `pipeline/measure/measure_eval_error.py` | See the distinction below. |
| **Measurement output** (CSV/log produced by the tools above) | `results/*.csv` (5 files), `results/scripts/gen1_master_measure.log`, `results/scripts/gen2_master_measure.log` | Data derived from measurement, not training data. |
| **Prose/documentation** | `README.md`, `LINEAGE.md`, `RESULTS.md`, `COMPLIANCE.md` (this file), `non_conforme/README.md` | Discuss the comparisons above, not pipeline code. |

**Distinction applied throughout this repository**: a **measurement tool**
reads or produces a reference value to compute an offline metric
(Spearman, MAE) and never writes to a file that later feeds training. A
**label source** writes `eval_cp`/`bestmove`/WDL to a file the training
pipeline reads. The measurement tools above are exactly and only that:
removing them from the repository wouldn't change a single bit of any
produced network, because they never wrote a training datum.

**It is not true, as an earlier version of this document claimed, that
Stockfish "never appears" in `pipeline/annotate/` and
`pipeline/generate/`** — it appears in both, for the reasons listed above
(gen0 moved to `non_conforme/`, gen1's declared opening filter). What
remains true, and verifiable line by line against the table above, is
that **no label of any presented network (gen1, gen2, gen3) comes from
Stockfish.**

## `non_conforme/`

Contains gen0 (a network trained on data with Stockfish labels, predating
knowledge of this rule) as a historical reference. It is not an ancestor
of any presented network — see `LINEAGE.md` and `non_conforme/README.md`
for details.

## Declaration

The `luna_gen1.nnue` and `luna_gen2.nnue` networks (and, once complete and
measured, `luna_gen3.nnue`) are trained exclusively on data generated by
the engine's own search/evaluation, following the bootstrap chain
documented in `LINEAGE.md`. No gen0 position or label, and none from any
external engine, entered their training data.
